title: Examining the Implication of Service Quality on Visitor Perception at a Recreational Park in Johor Bahru, Malaysia
content:
Visitors perceived the recreational park's physical facilities positively, while reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy fell below the neutral level. The findings highlight the need for improvements in delivery service and visitor support to enhance the overall recreational park experience.


ABSTRACT

This study aimed to assess visitors' perceptions of service quality at a recreational park in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, using a modified SERVQUAL model. The study examined five service quality dimensions, namely tangibility, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy, to determine visitors' perceptions of the services provided by the recreational park. A quantitative research approach was adopted, and data were collected from 382 visitors who experienced recreational park services in Johor Bahru. A structured questionnaire was used to collect information on respondents' demographic characteristics and their perceptions of the five SERVQUAL dimensions. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a one-sample t-test, with a test value of 3.00 representing the neutral midpoint of the five-point Likert scale. The findings showed that tangibility recorded a mean score of 3.445 and was significantly higher than the neutral value (p < 0.001). In contrast, reliability (M = 2.886, p = 0.001), responsiveness (M = 1.648, p < 0.001), assurance (M = 1.474, p < 0.001), and empathy (M = 2.063, p < 0.001) were significantly lower than the neutral value. Overall, the findings indicate that visitors perceived the physical aspects of the recreational park more positively, while reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy were perceived below the neutral level. These findings highlight specific areas of service quality that recreational park operators may consider improving to enhance the overall visitor experience and strengthen service delivery.
